title: dict.get()
summary: Return the value for `key`, or `default` when the key is absent — without raising.
description: The safe alternative to `d[key]`. Choose deliberately: `d[key]` asserts the key must be present, and its KeyError is a useful bug report. `.get` says absence is expected.

parameters.name: default
parameters.description: Returned when the key is missing.

real_world_usage: Reading optional fields from parsed JSON, applying configuration defaults, counting.

common_mistakes.fix: The default is not stored in the dict, so the append is lost. Use setdefault or defaultdict.
A silent None flowing three layers down is harder to debug than a KeyError at the source.

performance_notes: O(1) average, marginally slower than `d[key]` because of the default handling.
